1.title: Responding in Defender for Endpoint
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Responding in Defender for Endpoint. It covers the exam area two. Respond to security incidents. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Investigate device timelines. Perform actions on the device, including live response and collecting investigation packages. Perform evidence and entity investigation. Investigate and remediate incidents identified by automatic attack disruption. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two. Respond to security incidents (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: The device page and the timeline
1.text: The device page and the timeline. Open a device from Assets, then Devices, from an alert, or by global search.

1.title: The device page and the timeline, continued
1.text: The device page and the timeline. The figure shows this: Device page tabs and the response actions of a device.

1.title: The device page and the timeline, continued
1.text: The device page and the timeline. Overview. Active alerts, logged on users (past thirty days), security assessments, device health. Incidents and alerts. Alerts and incidents for the device. Timeline. Events on the device, in time order. Security recommendations, Software inventory, Discovered vulnerabilities, Missing K B s. Exposure data from vulnerability management. Default range. The past thirty days; filters for day, week, thirty days or a custom range. Export. Up to seven days of events. Flags. Flag key events to build a clean breach timeline. Hunt for related events. Opens advanced hunting. Exam tip: The timeline shows what happened on a device; flag the events that tell the attack story.

1.title: Response actions on a device
1.text: Response actions on a device. Manage tags. Labels the device (also used in dynamic scopes). Initiate live response session. A remote command-line session. Collect investigation package. Gathers forensic data into a zip. Run antivirus scan. Quick or full; default C P U cap fifty percent. Restrict app execution. Allows only Microsoft-signed apps, using a code integrity policy; undo with Remove app restrictions. Isolate device. Full or selective isolation. Contain device. Blocks communication with the device from all onboarded devices. Consult a threat expert. Microsoft Threat Experts.

1.title: Response actions on a device, continued
1.text: Response actions on a device. Plan one includes the manual actions run antivirus scan, isolate device, stop and quarantine a file, add an indicator; the others need Plan two. Full. Disconnects the device from the network; Defender service connectivity stays. Selective. Windows ten seventeen oh nine or later; can keep Outlook and Teams with isolation exclusions. Role. Active remediation actions. Offline device. Isolation is retried for up to three days. V P N (virtual private network). A full tunnel blocks the Defender cloud; use split tunneling. Contain device: Microsoft recommends up to one hundred devices at a time; it takes up to five minutes to propagate; undo with Release from containment. Exam tip: Isolate equals this device is cut off. Contain equals other devices stop talking to it (also used by attack disruption).

1.title: Investigation package
1.text: Investigation package. Choose Collect investigation package, enter a comment, and the zip downloads (or download from Action center). Windows contents. System. Autoruns, Installed programs, Processes, Services, Scheduled tasks, System information, Users and groups. Network. Network connections (Active Net Connections, A R P, D N S cache, I P config, firewall logs), S M B (Server Message Block) sessions. Evidence. Prefetch files, Security event log, Temp directories, Wd Support Logs, Collection Summary Report.xls.

1.title: Live response
1.text: Live response. Start: Device inventory, then device, then Initiate live response session. It must be turned on in Settings, then Endpoints, then Advanced features (and live response for servers). Basic and advanced commands are separate permissions in an R back custom role. cd, cls, connect, connections, dir, drivers, fg, fileinfo, findfile, getfile, help, jobs, persistence, processes, registry, scheduledtasks, services, startupfolders, status, trace. analyze, run, library, putfile, remediate, undo (plus collect, scan, isolate and release on mac O S or Linux).

1.title: Live response, continued
1.text: Live response. getfile. Download a file from the device. putfile. Send a library file to the device. run. Run a script from the library (do not use; and. remediate. Remove a file (delete), process (stop and delete), service, registry entry, scheduled task or startup item; undo reverts. Concurrent sessions. fifty per organization; five per user; one per device. Inactivity timeout. thirty minutes. Command timeout. ten minutes (thirty minutes for getfile, findfile, run). File sizes. getfile three gigabytes; library two hundred fifty megabytes; putfile three hundred megabytes on Windows. Background jobs. Add and to getfile or run; fg brings it back.

1.title: Live response, continued
1.text: Live response. Unsigned Power Shell scripts need the separate advanced feature Allow unsigned script execution in live response. Exam tip: Advanced live response is needed for run, putfile, library and remediate. getfile is basic.

1.title: Evidence and entity investigation
1.text: Evidence and entity investigation. File page. Observed in organization (devices up to six months, cloud apps thirty days); actions Stop and quarantine, Manage indicator, Download file, Collect file, Go hunt, Deep analysis. I P page. Geo information, related alerts, activity on up to one hundred devices, prevalence (default thirty days). Domain or U R L page. Verdict, incidents and alerts, devices, emails and clicks (last thirty days). User page. Overview, Alerts, Observed in organization; the dashboard shows Users at risk.

1.title: Evidence and entity investigation, continued
1.text: Evidence and entity investigation. Stop and quarantine file: Windows ten seventeen oh three or later; not for trusted non-Microsoft or Microsoft-signed files; up to one thousand devices; times out after three days. Download file gives a password-protected zip and needs Download quarantined files. Deep analysis works on P E files only. Evidence verdicts are Malicious, Suspicious, No threats found.

1.title: Incidents from automatic attack disruption
1.text: Incidents from automatic attack disruption. Incidents tagged Attack Disruption show the containment actions (Module four). The analyst checks the timeline, keeps the containment while investigating, removes the threat, then releases the device or user from the Action center.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A device shows ransomware activity. The sock wants to cut it off from the network but keep it reporting to Defender. Which action fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Isolate device, with full isolation of the network traffic. Full isolation disconnects the device from the network but keeps Defender service connectivity.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. An analyst needs Autoruns, prefetch files, services and the security event log from a suspected device for forensic review. What should the analyst use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Collect investigation package, then download the zip file. The investigation package gathers those forensic items into a zip.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An analyst wants to run a prepared script from the live response library on a device. Which command and permission apply? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The run command with advanced live response. Run needs advanced live response; getfile and cd are basic commands.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A user already has five live response sessions open and tries a sixth. What happens? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The sixth session is blocked because the limit is five per user. The limits are fifty concurrent sessions per organization and five per user.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An analyst chooses Stop and quarantine for a file signed by Microsoft. What is the result? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The action is not available for Microsoft-signed files. Stop and quarantine cannot be applied to trusted non-Microsoft or Microsoft-signed files.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. What does the Restrict app execution action do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Allows only Microsoft-signed apps through a code integrity policy. Restrict app execution applies a policy that allows only Microsoft-signed files.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many live response sessions can one user have? Answer: Five at the same time. Question two. What is the getfile size limit? Answer: three gigabytes. Question three. How long is the live response inactivity timeout? Answer: thirty minutes.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which role is needed to isolate a device? Answer: Active remediation actions. Question five. Which file type does deep analysis support? Answer: P E files only. Question six. How long can the timeline be exported? Answer: Up to seven days.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Timeline: default thirty days; flag events; export seven days. Actions: live response, investigation package, scan, restrict app, isolate, contain. Isolate versus contain: isolate cuts the device off; contain blocks others from reaching it. Live response: fifty sessions, five per user, thirty minutes idle; advanced for run, putfile, library, remediate. Limits: getfile three gigabytes, library two hundred fifty megabytes, putfile three hundred megabytes. File actions: stop and quarantine (one thousand devices, not Microsoft-signed), download, collect, deep analysis.
